question: The Audit Authority within the Romanian Court of Accounts is responsible for the audit of EU funds in Romania and is bound by European and national rules to be independent of any political parties.

The Ethics Code of the Romanian Court of Accounts (Article 24(j)) stipulates that disciplinary misconduct includes, among other things, ‘public expression of political opinions or beliefs, as well as participation in activities or public events of a political nature’.

However, according to media reports, Eugen Teodorovici, a former finance minister and current director of the Audit Authority within the Romanian Court of Accounts, was involved in the recent launch of the Sovereignist Bloc, an alliance of political parties.
This is despite the regulations in place and the Court’s Code of Ethics, which explicitly forbid members from expressing political opinions or engaging in political activities.

Without an independent Audit Authority, Romania cannot provide an effective and efficient internal control system, which is in direct violation of European regulations, including Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2021/241 establishing the Recovery and Resilience Facility. 1.
Is the Commission aware of the above-mentioned situation in Romania?
What is the Commission’s assessment of the situation?
Is the Commission planning on taking action on this matter?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.6.2024) The Financing and Loan Agreements for the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) signed with Romania1 set out the key requirements of the control system referred to in article 22(1) of the RRF Regulation, including the independence of audit functions.

In this respect, the Commission shall be sufficiently assured that Romania’s internal control system fulfils the key requirements. At the same time, in relation to the Cohesion policy, implemented under shared management, Regulation (EU) 2021/10602 establishes clear requirements related to the management and control system, that includes an independent audit authority.

The Commission has already analysed the independence of the Audit Authority within the Romanian Court of Accounts at the moment of the assessment of the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) and will continue to monitor this in the context of future system audits and compliance audits.

The Commission understands that the situation described in relation to one of the Directors of the Audit Authority is currently being addressed through an investigation launched at the beginning of March 2024 by the Ethics Committee within the Audit Authority.

In any event, the audits issued by the Audit Authority on the RRP and on the cohesion programmes are being subject to quality control procedures and endorsed by the President and responsible Vice-Presidents. Upon the completion of internal procedures at the level of the Audit Authority, the Commission will decide if any additional measures are to be implemented.
